statements.status_notes: CVE-2008-1688: GNU m4 before 1.4.11 passed the file name given to the -F (freeze state) option to a printf-style error reporter as the format string, so a crafted file name could lead to arbitrary code execution when the frozen file could not be written. GNU m4 fixed this in 1.4.11 (upstream commit 'Security fix: avoid arbitrary code execution with m4 -F', https://lists.libreplanet.org/archive/html/m4-commit/2007-11/msg00027.html, recorded in the 1.4.11 NEWS entry on security fixes for the -F option). This package is built from upstream m4 1.4.19, whose src/freeze.c reports the open failure with a fixed format string and passes the file name as an argument (https://sources.debian.org/src/m4/1.4.19-8/src/freeze.c/). Every published build of this package is based on 1.4.19 and contains the fix; the range boundary is the currently published package version. Debian's tracker records no fixed version because it rates the issue unimportant (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2008-1688).
